answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a dated service-commitment market. Each identity posts a priced, dated promise - a mirror of its real capacity - and locks escrow behind it. A stranger claims the commitment; on delivery the escrow returns plus a fee, but a missed deadline forfeits the bond and writes a public default record, dark as sable, into the identity's permanent history. Clones must each post fresh escrow and either do real work or burn money, while an onyx-hard rule caps live commitments per identity, so scaling an army costs linearly in escrow, time and reputation.
